title: Fraught
summary: FRAUGHT, adjective fraut. 1. Laden; loaded; charged; as a vessel richly fraught with goods from India. This sense is used in poetry; but in common business, freighted only is used. 2. Filled; stored;

inlines.v: FRAUGHT, adjective fraut. 1. Laden; loaded; charged; as a vessel richly fraught with goods from India. This sense is used in poetry; but in common business, freighted only is used. 2. Filled; stored; full; as a scheme fraught with mischief; the scriptures are fraught with excellent precepts. FRAUGHT, noun A freight; a cargo. [Not now used.] FRAUGHT, verb transitive To load; to fill; to crowd. obsolete
